small_guidance:
- Sweep BLOCK_W ∈ {16, 32, 64} and num_warps ∈ {2, 4, 8} via `triton.autotune` on `(OD, OH, OW, N)` — with OW=33, BLOCK_W=16 gives 3 tiles vs BLOCK_W=32's 2 tiles with heavy tail-masking; an aligned BLOCK_W choice can save ~15-25% of stride-2 wasted lanes.
- Hoist the input gather: since stride=2, only ~1/8 of `(kd,kh,kw)` combinations contribute valid input at any output cell. Replace the 27-iter `static_range` triple loop with two static loops over `(kd_parity, kh_parity, kw_parity)` collapsed — i.e. compute `id_q` once per parity and skip the divisibility check. This removes ~26/27 of the masked loads.
- Try `num_stages=3` and pre-load the full weight tile `w[IC, OC, KD, KH, KW]` once into registers (only 3·16·27=1296 floats) outside the spatial loops, then index it with constexpr offsets — cuts weight-load traffic from KDHW×OC loads per program to one.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a scatter-add ConvTranspose: launch over `(N, ID, IH, IW)` input tiles, compute the `[OC, BLOCK]` outer product `weight @ x` into a per-program output patch, then `tl.atomic_add` into the full conv output. This eliminates the stride-2 wasted-iteration problem entirely (every kernel iteration does useful work). Follow with a separate fused LSE+HardSwish+bias+clamp kernel reading `[N,OC,OD,OH,OW]`.
- Alternatively, split into two kernels: (1) a true GEMM-based ConvTranspose3d producing `[N, OC, OD, OH, OW]` with `BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=IC*KD*KH*KW=81` using channels-last layout, then (2) a row-wise fused LSE/HardSwish/clamp kernel over the OC axis. Current per-output gather forces redundant weight loads and wastes 7/8 of stride-2 iterations.
- If staying with the gather strategy, switch the inner-most contraction to `tl.dot` with weight laid out as `[KD*KH*KW, IC, OC]` precomputed in `__init__` (a layout-only transform, not algebraic), enabling a single `tl.dot(x_tile[BLOCK_W, IC], w_tile[IC, OC])` per (kd,kh,kw) — Tensor Cores will outperform the current FMA-only outer product.
